chunks: Sa'd from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ayoub ibn Nuh from Safwan ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Sayrafī from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from whomsoever he narrated, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him):
Regarding a man who prays in a sock (khuff) that has become dirty, he said: 'If it is of a type in which prayer is not completed, there is no objection.'

key_terms.الْخُفِّ: A leather sock or footwear worn over the feet, commonly used in Shia jurisprudence for wiping during ablution.
key_terms.قَذَرٌ: Dirt or impurity (najasah) that may affect ritual purity.
key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ: There is no objection / it is permissible.
key_terms.يَتِمُّ فِيهِ الصَّلَاةَ: In which the prayer is completed/performed fully.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying in footwear that has become dirty or impure?
ai.summary: Reported through the chain of Safwan ibn Yahya, a key figure in the Shia hadith transmission, this narration clarifies the fiqh of khuff (leather socks) by distinguishing between impurities that break wudu and those that do not. It establishes that minor dirt or impurity on the footwear does not invalidate the prayer, reflecting the Shia principle that the garment must be pure but minor defects do not nullify the act of worship.
